customer_jane: Hey team — after our IdP rotated signing certs this morning our users started seeing 403 on login to app. Worked until ~08:12 UTC. Not seeing anything obvious on our side. Any idea?

sam_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Jane. Can you paste the exact SAML error you see or a screenshot? Is this for all users or specific SP/tenant?

customer_jane: All users across the tenant. Error in SP logs: "saml: assertion recipient mismatch or signature invalid". We also see some 403s in front door logs with request id `fd-9a1b`. Trying to repro, I fetched the IdP metadata and got something odd — looks binary.

customer_jane: (paste) `curl -i https://idp.examplecorp.com/metadata`

customer_jane: Response headers: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nContent-Type: application/xml\nContent-Length: 842` and the body begins with `\x1f\x8b\x08` (looks gzipped)

sam_support: Hmm — metadata body is gzipped but Content-Encoding header missing. That could make our metadata fetcher parse raw gzip bytes as XML and fail to pick up the new KeyDescriptor nodes. Are you able to share the raw curl output (or let us fetch it from our side)?

customer_jane: I can paste a hexdump snippet: `0000000: 1f8b 0800 0000 0000 00ff`

alex_infra: Looping in infra — @maria_sre fyi. We have a metadata poller that expects either Content-Encoding: gzip/brotli or plain XML. If server returns gzipped payload without header, our HTTP client returns compressed bytes which then break the XML parser. That could cause us to keep an older cached metadata (with old cert) or fail parse entirely.

maria_sre: On it. @alex_infra can you check our metadata fetch logs for that tenant? I want to see whether our fetcher logged a parse error or used cached metadata.

deploy-bot: [metadata-poller] 1865432115 tenant=examplecorp fetch=200 parse_error=unexpected token 0x1f at offset 0 cached_fallback=true

alex_infra: Confirmed in logs: fetch returned 200 but parse failed with `unexpected token 0x1f` and we fell back to cached metadata (old cert). That explains signature mismatch after IdP rotated cert.

sam_support: Thanks. Two paths: short-term workaround + long-term fix. Short-term: can you upload the IdP metadata manually in Console > Integrations > SAML for tenant, or ask IdP to add `Content-Encoding: gzip` header or serve uncompressed? Which do you prefer?

customer_jane: We'll ask IdP to add header but that'll take them ~30–45m. Can we upload manual metadata to avoid user impact?

maria_sre: Yes — manual upload will bypass our poller cache and immediately use correct keys. If you upload, make sure to decompress the metadata first. Steps: `curl -s https://idp.examplecorp.com/metadata | gunzip -c > idp-metadata.xml` then upload idp-metadata.xml in Console.

customer_jane: Doing that now. Upload complete. Testing... login successful for one user. Rolling out to rest. Thanks.

alex_infra: For the long-term, I'll open a hotfix: make poller detect gzip magic bytes (0x1f 0x8b) and attempt to gunzip even if Content-Encoding missing, and log a telemetry event for unexpected encodings. Also add a retry path that rejects parse and fails fast instead of silently falling back to old cached metadata.

maria_sre: Agreed. Also add a health alert if parse_error=true and cached_fallback=true, since falling back silently is risky during cert rotations.

alex_infra: I'll push PR shortly and schedule hotfix to prod. Tentative plan: branch+test in canary region -> prod hotfix within 2 hours. Will update thread with PR link.

deploy-bot: [ci] build triggered for refs/heads/metadata-gzip-detect (pr #4521)

alex_infra: PR 4521: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/metadata-poller/pulls/4521 — adds gzip magic detection, gunzip fallback, improved logging, and a metric `metadata.fetch.encoding_mismatch`

sam_support: Great. Jane — once hotfix rolls, we can remove manual upload and re-enable poller if you prefer automatic metadata. Otherwise keeping manual upload is fine until IdP fixes headers.

customer_jane: We'll keep manual upload for now and coordinate with IdP to fix headers. Appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup:

maria_sre: Closing loop: hotfix merged and deployed to canary at 09:20 UTC, prod rollout started 09:45 UTC, monitoring shows `metadata.fetch.parse_error` rate dropped to 0 and `metadata.fetch.encoding_mismatch` metric spiked (good signal). Marking resolved.

sam_support: Marking thread resolved — reopen if issues recur.
